metadata.title: Closedness and attractive approximation of binary MTP2 edge models
metadata.description:
For every fixed finite simple graph, this research note proves that the binary MTP2 probability distributions admitting finite nonnegative unary and original-edge factors are exactly the pointwise limits of strictly positive attractive Ising distributions on the same graph. It consequently answers Conjecture 1 in Lauritzen's 2022 Oberwolfach problem statement affirmatively, including zero probabilities and the source's literal edge-only conventions for isolated vertices and empty graphs. The proof explicitly handles pins, deterministic equalities and implication supports, aggregates interactions across equality classes, constructs positive attractive approximations, and uses a classical residual-flow representation to bound finite factors with a nonvanishing normalizer.

The note credits the toric support framework of Geiger, Meek and Sturmfels, the MTP2 graphical results of Lauritzen, Uhler and Zwiernik and Fallat et al., the natural-support factorization framework of Kahle and Sullivant, and classical graph-cut and residual-flow tools. The supplement gives the additional facial-lattice support derivation underlying the comparison. The accompanying negative answers to the separate factorization conjectures are credited to the exact earlier counterexample of Gandolfi and Lenarda, published April 13, 2017. No new-counterexample, first-discovery or exhaustive historical-priority claim is made. Portable exact verification code and generated results accompany the proofs; bounded finite checks do not replace the arbitrary-graph proof.

This is an unrefereed preprint. AI tools were used extensively in developing the arguments, searching primary literature, writing, coding, reproduction and independent adversarial review. Automated reviews and exact computations are not external human peer review or formal proof-assistant certification; neither is claimed.
